records.benefit: A monthly food benefit on a QUEST card. The amount depends on household size, income, and expenses.
eligibilityCaveats: Adults aged 18-52 without dependents may need to meet work requirements to keep benefits beyond three months.
Some households face an asset limit. Most do not, but it is checked during the application.
Immigration status affects eligibility for some household members. Children are often eligible even when adults are not.

If your household includes someone who is elderly, blind, or disabled, you may still qualify even with gross income above 200% of the poverty line — a different rule based on income after deductions applies. Check with your county agency or ACCESS Wisconsin.

steps: Apply online through ACCESS Wisconsin, by phone, or in person at your county agency.
Complete an interview, usually by phone.
Send proof of income and expenses if asked.

records.name: FoodShare Wisconsin (SNAP)
requiredDocuments: Proof of income for everyone in the household
Proof of housing and utility costs
records.summary: Wisconsin’s version of SNAP, once called food stamps. Money is loaded onto a QUEST card each month that you use like a debit card at grocery stores and many farmers markets.

records.benefit: A monthly benefit for specific foods — milk, eggs, produce, infant formula, whole grains — plus nutrition counseling and health referrals.
eligibilityCaveats: A WIC clinic also checks for a nutritional or medical need at the first appointment. Most applicants meet this.
Fathers, grandparents, and foster parents can apply on behalf of an eligible child.

steps: Call the Madison and Dane County WIC office (or your county’s WIC agency if outside Dane County) to book an appointment.
Bring ID, proof of address, and proof of income.
Attend a short appointment where height, weight, and iron levels are checked.

records.name: Wisconsin WIC
records.summary: Nutrition support for pregnant people, new parents, infants, and children under 5. WIC covers specific healthy foods, plus breastfeeding support and nutrition checkups.

records.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction and your school district
records.benefit: Free or reduced-price school breakfast and lunch during the school year.
eligibilityCaveats: Below 130% of the poverty level meals are free; between 130% and 185% they are reduced-price.
Some Wisconsin schools serve free meals to every student regardless of income. Check with your district first.
Households already receiving FoodShare are usually enrolled automatically.

steps: Get the household application from your district, usually online or in the enrollment packet.
List every child and the household income.
Return it to the school. You can apply at any point in the school year.

records.name: Free and Reduced-Price School Meals
records.summary: Free or low-cost breakfast and lunch at school for children in households under the income limit. One application covers every child in the household.

records.benefit: A summer grocery benefit per eligible child, on a card usable at grocery stores.
eligibilityCaveats: Most eligible children are enrolled automatically — the state matches records from FoodShare, W-2, Medicaid, and school meal applications. Apply directly only if you are not contacted and believe your child qualifies.

The child must attend a school that takes part in the National School Lunch Program. Children at schools that don’t (including homeschooled or fully virtual students) cannot get this through a direct application — check with the school.

steps: Check whether your child was already enrolled automatically — most eligible children are.
If not, and your child’s school participates in the National School Lunch Program, apply directly online during the summer application window.

records.name: Summer EBT (SUN Bucks)
records.seasonalNote: Benefits are issued over the summer and the direct-application window is limited.
records.summary: A summer grocery benefit for school-age children, meant to replace the school meals they lose when classes are out.

records.administeredBy: Second Harvest Foodbank of Southern Wisconsin
records.benefit: Free groceries from a local pantry or mobile distribution. They also help people apply for FoodShare.
eligibilityCaveats: Second Harvest also serves Adams, Columbia, Crawford, Dodge, Grant, Green, Iowa, Jefferson, Juneau, Lafayette, Monroe, Richland, Rock, Sauk, and Vernon counties — if you live in one of those, you are also covered even though this tool only checked Dane County.
Individual pantries may set their own limits on how often you can visit, or ask for proof of address.
Their FoodShare outreach team will help you apply for SNAP for free, over the phone.

steps: Use the pantry finder to locate a site near you and check its hours.
Go during open hours. Most sites do not need an appointment.

records.name: Second Harvest Foodbank of Southern Wisconsin

source.name: Second Harvest Foodbank of Southern Wisconsin

records.summary: A network of food pantries and mobile food distributions across a 16-county region of southern Wisconsin, including Dane County. No income test and no application — pantries are open to anyone who needs food.

records.benefit: Weekly groceries, take-home prepared meals, community meals, and a mobile delivery route for people who cannot travel to the pantry.
eligibilityCaveats: Groceries and FAM take-home meals require self-attesting that your household income is at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level (Wisconsin’s TEFAP guideline) — no proof is required. This does not appear to apply to their on-site Community Meals.
You can pick up groceries and FAM meals once per week; their week runs Tuesday through Friday.
New clients register online (ePantry / curbside registration) or in person; the site does not specify a documentation requirement.

steps: Check the current hours on their site — they change seasonally.
Register as a new client online, or come during open hours. No appointment or referral is needed.

records.name: The River Food Pantry
records.summary: Dane County’s busiest food pantry. Groceries, take-home and mobile meals, and no referral needed — but groceries and take-home meals do require self-attesting your income, unlike a typical no-questions-asked pantry.

records.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Administration, through local agencies
records.benefit: A one-time annual payment toward heating costs, plus a separate electric benefit. The amount depends on income, household size, fuel type, and energy use.

of.note: WHEAP looks at your income from the most recent month, not the whole year, so a recent drop can still qualify you. Contact your county energy agency to check.

eligibilityCaveats: Income is counted from the most recent month, annualized, not the whole year, so a recent drop in income can qualify you even if the annual figure above does not. Tell us if your income has recently dropped and we will flag this for you.
Renters qualify even when heat is included in the rent.
You can receive this once per heating season.
Funding is limited each program year. When it runs out, no more benefits are issued for that year even to households who qualify.

steps: Find the agency for your county — in Dane County this is Energy Services of Dane County.
Apply online, by phone, or in person.
Provide proof of income for the last three months and a recent energy bill.

records.name: Wisconsin Home Energy Assistance Program (WHEAP)
requiredDocuments: Proof of income for the last three months for everyone 18 and over
A recent heating and electric bill
Social Security numbers for household members
records.seasonalNote: The regular heating season runs from October 1 through May 15.

source.name: Wisconsin Energy and Housing — Energy Assistance

records.summary: A once-a-year payment toward your heating and electric costs. The money goes straight to your energy company, not to you.

records.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Administration, through local agencies
records.benefit: Emergency payment to restore or keep service, and repair or replacement of a broken furnace for homeowners. Available 24 hours a day.

of.note: WHEAP looks at your income from the most recent month, not the whole year, so a recent drop can still qualify you. Contact your county energy agency to check.

eligibilityCaveats: You generally need to qualify for regular WHEAP first, and can apply for both at the same time.
Furnace repair and replacement is for homeowners. Renters should contact their local agency, which will work with the landlord.
Wisconsin also bans heat disconnection from November 1 to April 15 for residential customers, separately from this program.

steps: Call your county agency right away — do not wait for the regular application.
Explain that you have a shutoff notice or no heat.
Emergency situations are handled outside normal office hours.

records.name: WHEAP Crisis Assistance and Emergency Furnace Repair

source.name: Wisconsin Energy and Housing — Crisis Assistance

records.summary: Emergency help when your heat has been shut off, is about to be, or your furnace has stopped working. This moves much faster than the regular energy assistance process.

records.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Administration, through local agencies
records.benefit: Free energy audit and home improvements. There is no cost to the household and nothing to repay.

of.note: This program's income test may look at recent income rather than the full year, so a recent drop may still qualify you. Contact your local weatherization agency to check.

eligibilityCaveats: Renters need the property owner’s written consent before work can start.
Households already receiving WHEAP are usually automatically income-eligible.
There is often a waiting list, and homes with the highest energy use are usually prioritised.

steps: Contact the weatherization agency serving your county.
Complete an application and provide proof of income.
An auditor visits to assess the home and decide what work is needed.

records.name: Wisconsin Weatherization Assistance Program
records.summary: Free home energy improvements — insulation, air sealing, furnace repair or replacement — to permanently lower your energy bills. Renters qualify too, with the landlord’s consent.

records.administeredBy: Community Development Authority of the City of Madison
records.benefit: Ongoing monthly rent assistance paid to your landlord.

of.note: The Section 8 waiting list has been closed to new applications since April 2023. The CDA is not currently accepting applications; check cityofmadison.com/dpced/housing/applicants for a reopening.

eligibilityCaveats: Applicants do not need to currently live in the City of Madison, but Madison residents get application preference when a list is open.
Waits are commonly measured in years once a list opens.
A criminal background check and rental history review are part of the process.
Vouchers can usually be transferred to another housing authority after the first year.

steps: Check whether the waiting list is currently open — it has been closed since April 2023.
Apply online while it is open — the window is often short.
Keep your contact details current; applications are removed if the CDA cannot reach you.

records.name: Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8)
records.seasonalNote: The Section 8 voucher waiting list has been closed to new applications since April 2023. (The CDA’s separate public housing waiting list is open; this record covers Section 8 vouchers only.)

source.name: City of Madison CDA Housing — Applicants

records.summary: A voucher that pays part of your rent directly to a private landlord. You find the apartment; the voucher covers the difference between roughly 30% of your income and the rent. The waiting list has been closed since 2023 — this is a lead to check on, not an active program to apply to today.

records.benefit: A monthly credit of up to $30 on your municipal services bill. Never needs to be repaid.
eligibilityCaveats: You must apply — eligible households are not enrolled automatically — and reapply every year.
The account generally has to be in your name at your current Madison address.
Unpaid municipal services bills are placed on the property tax roll, so this matters for homeowners as well as renters.
If you are behind on your bill or facing a shutoff, call Madison Water Utility about a payment plan separately from applying for this credit.

steps: Gather income verification — a tax return, Social Security statement, or proof you receive FoodShare, a Housing Choice Voucher, or WIC.
Apply online or print and submit the PDF application.

records.name: Madison Customer Assistance Program (MadCAP)

source.name: City of Madison — Madison Customer Assistance Program (MadCAP)

records.summary: A monthly credit on your City of Madison municipal services bill (water, sewer, stormwater, and urban forestry charges) for low-income households. You have to apply and reapply every year — it is not automatic.

records.administeredBy: Tenant Resource Center, with Dane County and City of Madison funding
records.benefit: One-time payment toward back rent or a security deposit, plus free tenant counseling and help communicating with a landlord.

of.note: Income limits and funding availability change and are not published in a way we can check automatically. Contact the Tenant Resource Center to find out whether you qualify.

eligibilityCaveats: Funding is limited and runs out at points during the year. Apply as early as you can.
You usually need a lease or a written demand for rent, plus a landlord willing to accept payment.
Tenant counseling is free and available to everyone regardless of income — call even if you do not qualify for the payment.

steps: Call the housing help desk, or start online.
Have your lease, your eviction notice if you have one, and proof of income ready.
A counselor will talk through your options, including ones that are not money.

records.name: Eviction Prevention and Rent Assistance
records.summary: Help paying overdue rent, and free advice on your rights as a tenant, for people at risk of losing their housing in Dane County.

records.administeredBy: Federal Communications Commission, via the Universal Service Administrative Company
records.benefit: A monthly discount of up to $9.25 on one phone or internet bill per household, with a larger discount on Tribal lands.
eligibilityCaveats: One discount per household, not per person.
You must recertify each year or the discount stops.
You choose a participating provider; not every carrier takes part.

steps: Check that a participating provider serves your address.
Apply online through the National Verifier.
Contact the provider you chose to apply the discount to your bill.

records.name: Lifeline (phone and internet discount)
requiredDocuments: Proof of income or proof of benefit enrollment

source.name: Lifeline Support — Universal Service Administrative Company

records.summary: A monthly discount on phone or internet service. Available in every state, including for people who move.

records.benefit: Full health insurance: doctor visits, prescriptions, urgent and emergency care, lab tests, mental health care, and more, through a ForwardHealth card.
eligibilityCaveats: Adults — both parents/caretaker relatives and adults without children — are capped at 100% of the federal poverty level regardless of household composition. Only pregnant people and children under 19 qualify up to 306% FPL, so at some income levels only your children may qualify, not you. Apply anyway.
Children ages 1–18 with family income over 201% FPL are charged a monthly premium (no more than 5% of counted income). Coverage does not end for not paying it.
Covers ages 0–64 only. If everyone in the household is 65 or older, or needs disability- or long-term-care-related Medicaid, a different pathway applies — contact your agency.

A new federal work requirement (from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) starts affecting some members ages 19–64 beginning January 2027. Pregnant people, parents/caretakers of a child under 19, people with disabilities, and several other groups are exempt.
Immigration status affects eligibility for some household members. Children are often eligible even when adults are not.

steps: Apply online through ACCESS Wisconsin, by phone, or in person at your county or Tribal agency — there is no enrollment period, so you can apply any time.
Have Social Security numbers, income, and household details ready for everyone applying.
After approval, you will get a ForwardHealth card in the mail.

records.name: BadgerCare Plus
records.summary: Wisconsin’s Medicaid program — full health coverage for people ages 0–64 with low income, including pregnant people, children, parents, and caretaker relatives. There is no enrollment period; you can apply any time.

records.administeredBy: Wisconsin Department of Children and Families
records.benefit: A monthly child care subsidy covering part of your child care costs. The amount depends on your family’s size, income, and approved activity hours.

of.note: Wisconsin Shares requires a parent or caregiver to be working, in school, or in an approved job-training or W-2/FoodShare Employment and Training activity. Contact your local agency to confirm your activity qualifies.

eligibilityCaveats: A parent, foster parent, or kinship caregiver must be working, attending school, or in an approved job-training, apprenticeship, or W-2/FoodShare Employment and Training (FSET) activity to receive the subsidy.

Children must be under 13, or under 19 if the child has a disability, to qualify. This app’s "school-age child" answer covers ages 5–18 (K–12), which is broader than that cutoff — if your only child is a teenager 13 or older without a disability, you likely do not qualify even if this program appears.
Children receiving the subsidy must be U.S. citizens or qualifying immigrants; parents do not need to be.

Once approved, you can stay eligible until your income reaches 85% of the state median income, which is higher than the 200% FPL limit to first qualify — an income increase after enrolling usually does not end your subsidy right away.
The child care provider must be licensed, certified, or operated by a Wisconsin public school board, and must have a YoungStar quality rating of at least 2 stars.

steps: Apply online through ACCESS Wisconsin, or contact your county or Tribal Income Maintenance agency to apply by phone or in person.
Complete an eligibility interview and report your family size, income, and approved activity.
After approval, complete a child care needs assessment within 30 days to set your subsidy amount.

records.name: Wisconsin Shares Child Care Subsidy

source.name: Wisconsin DCF — Wisconsin Shares for Parents and Caregivers

records.summary: Helps pay for child care so parents and caregivers can work, go to school, or take part in an approved job-training program. Funds are loaded onto an EBT card you use to pay your child care provider.

records.administeredBy: Dane County Department of Human Services
records.benefit: One-to-one help from a social worker who knows the local programs, including help filling out applications and small amounts of emergency assistance.
eligibilityCaveats: Workers are assigned by neighborhood, so which office you contact depends on where you live.
This is the best starting point if your situation does not fit neatly into any single program.

steps: Find the JFF office for your neighborhood using the county site’s office finder.
Explain your situation — there is no application form to start.

records.name: Joining Forces for Families

source.name: Dane County Human Services — Joining Forces for Families

records.summary: Neighborhood social workers who help Dane County residents find and apply for whatever they need — rent help, food, utilities, childcare, health care. Free, and you do not need to qualify for anything first.

records.benefit: A referral specialist who searches a database of local programs with you and makes warm handoffs. Available 24 hours a day.
eligibilityCaveats: This is a referral service, not a source of money itself.
Useful when nothing else here fits, or when a program has closed its waiting list.
Outside Wisconsin, dialing 211 reaches your own local referral service instead.

steps: Dial 211, or text your ZIP code to 898211.
Describe what you need.

records.name: 211 Wisconsin
records.summary: A free, confidential helpline that connects you to local assistance of any kind. Dial 211 from any phone, any time, in any language.
